programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Ladybird & Bee/Daolag-bhreac is Seillean
programme.desc: Tha tòrr bhèibidhean beaga daolag-bhreac rim frithealadh an-diugh. There are many ladybird babies to look after today.

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Tha Oona 's May ag argamaid, 's an dithis aca den bheachd gur iad as luaithe. Tha iad a cur romhpa rèis an aghaidh a chèile son co-dhùnadh a dhèanamh ach chan e Oona neo May a tha buannachadh aig deireadh an là ach farpaiseach mi-choltach! Oona and May get into an argument, both believing that they are faster than the other. They decide to race one another to see who is right, but they both end up being beaten by an unlikely competitor.

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Tha droch stoirm ag adhbharachadh bùrach uabhasach. Tha Oona 's Baba a cuideachadh le bhith sgioblachadh nuair a chi iad g' eil an t-s ide air Silky fhàgail àrd am measg nan creagan, gun dòigh faighinn air ais dhan fhairge 's gu teaghlach. A wild storm leaves puffin rock in a bit of a mess. As Oona and Baba prepare to help clean it up, they discover that the weather and high tides have left Silky stranded on the cliff with no way back to sea and her family.

programme.title: Boban is Fuigheag
programme.desc: Tha ’ad a' cluich tarraing an ròp an-diugh - no am b’ fheàrr tarraing an clò a-ràdh ris? Tha Fuigheag glè mhath air oir tha e nas làidire na shaoileadh tu. They’re playing tug of war today, or should it be called tug of tweed? Fuigheag is very good at it as he’s stronger than one thinks.

programme.title: Losgannan | Froglets
programme.desc: Cuiridh Ailig suas teanta agus thèid na Losgannan don fhàsach a rannsachadh phioramaidean. When Alex sets up a tent, the Froglets head into the desert as ancient pyramid explorers.

programme.title: Meaban and Moo
programme.desc: Bidh Linda a’ tadhal air a caraidean Meaban is Moo sa bhothan aca gus dùbhlain spòrsail a chur romhpa. Anns a’ phrògram seo tha na rionnagan a’ priobadh a-muigh agus tha Linda ag iarraidh air Meaban is Moo trì rudan ann an cumadh rionnaig a lorg. Tha treallaich gu leòr sa bhothan agus feumaidh iad a dhol a rùraich gus an lorg. Linda visits her friends Meaban and Moo at their hut to set them fun challenges. The stars are twinkling outside and Linda tasks Meaban and Moo with finding three star-shaped items. Their hut is full of junk so they need to have a good rummage!

programme.title: Dòtaman
programme.desc: Prògram Dòtaman bho 1990 air cuspair an tractor. Seinnibh an òran ainmeil "An Tractar a th'agamsa 's esan a tha thrang..." cuide ri Donnie agus tha sgeulachd is cleasachd gu leòr eile ri fhaotainnn. Coimheadibh airson Cagnaidh is Crotal, agus bithibh deiseal airson Nelson is Napoleon aig a' ghleoc! A classic treat from the Dotaman archives. Recorded in 1990, the programme explores the topic of the tractor. Sing along with Donnie to the iconic song, look out for furry friends Cagnaidh and Crotal and be prepared to count along with Nelson and Napoleon at the Dotaman clock!

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Catriona Nic a’ Phì a’ leughadh A Bhith nam Leòmhann. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh agus a dhealbhachadh le Emma Carlisle agus chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Jo NicDhòmhnaill. A bedtime story for young children. Catriona MacPhee reads A Bhith nam Leòmhann, written and illustrated by Emma Carlisle and translated into Gaelic by Jo Macdonald.

programme.title: An Teaghlach Rìoghail an Ath-dhoras/The Royals Next Door
programme.desc: Nuair nach eil fear a’ ghiotàr 'son cluich as a' chòmhlan aig Mìcheal aig seotha tàlant na sgoil’, tha Stella a' gabhail àit'. An dùil am bi i soirbheachail? When the guitar player doesn’t want to play in Mìcheal’s band at the school talent show, Stella takes his place. Will she be successful?

programme.title: An Teaghlach Rìoghail an Ath-dhoras/The Royals Next Door
programme.desc: Tha Stella ’son na Bànrigh a chuideachadh. Tha i airson gum bi i a’ dèanamh rudeigin àbhaisteach, mar gum bi i na ball den Chlub Leabhair. Ach, dè cho àbhaisteach sa tha e nuair a tha a’ Bhànrigh a' dol ann? Stella wants to help the Queen. She wants her to do something normal, like becoming a member of the Book Club. But how normal is it when the Queen attends?

programme.title: An Sgoil
programme.desc: Latha mòr dha Mgr Mackle le Mèar a’ bhaile a’ tighinn airson seann chlach na sgoile a chomharrachadh. Tha Daisy agus Danny trang a’ feuchainn ris a h-uile càil a chur air dòigh ach chan eil Mrs Fullerton neo na faoileagan a' cuideachadh ghnothaichean. A big day for Mr Mackle with the mayor coming to celebrate the school's ancient stone. Daisy and Danny are busy making sure that everything is in place, but Mrs Fullerton and the seagulls aren’t helping matters.

programme.title: Bogaisean is Gumbalan/Bottersnikes and Gumbles
programme.desc: Tha a h-uile neach tinn – ach Dùd a-mhàin – agus feumar a bhith còir nuair tha Gumbal bochd. Ach saoil a-nis ciamar a thèid leotha uile? Everyone but Dùd is sick, and everyone must care when a Gumbal is ill. How will they all get on?

programme.title: Bogaisean is Gumbalan/Bottersnikes and Gumbles
programme.desc: Tha Troig mì-fhoighidneach an-diugh - tha e searbh de bhith glacte sa mhagnat aig na Bògaisean ’s tha e dèanamh suas inntinn am magnat a ghoid. Chan eil an Rìgh toilichte idir ach tha Gubbo an dùil inneal a chruthachadh ‘son a’ mhagnait a ghluasad air ais. Troig is impatient today, he is fed up of being caught in the Bògaisean’s magnet once too often and he makes up his mind to steal it. The King is not at all happy but Gubbo intends to invent a machine to transport the magnet back.

programme.title: Fuine
programme.desc: Gregor samples a new take on custard creams. Griogar MacLeòid is eileanaich eile lem molaidhean son fuine bhlasta staigh agaibh pfhèin.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: We meet Gaelic learner Caroline Quinn from Trinidad and Tobago, while Calum Maclean is in Portmahomack, Easter Ross, learning about his heritage.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Mas Fhior
programme.desc: Niall Iain Macdonald hosts a new quiz show where more than general knowledge is required to win. Standing in the way of our two teams from winning are the Pretenders, who, from the comfort of their own homes, are on a mission to fox our contestants. Which of this week’s teams, Ross and Barry or Mairi and John, will get the upper hand and have a chance to take home the grand prize? Niall Iain Dòmhnallach le farpais cheist ùr far a bheil barrachd air eòlas coitcheann a dhìth gus buannachadh. Tha na Mas Fhìoraich a’ gabhail pàirt bhon dachaighean ’s ag amas air a’ chùis a dhèanamh air an dà sgioba. Cò aca bho sgiobaidhean na seachdain-sa, Ross & Barry no Mairi & John, a gheibh làmh an uachdar agus cothrom fhaighinn air an duais mhòr? In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Miann na Maighdinn-mara/Mermaid Tales
programme.desc: Tha maighdinn-mhara Innse Gall a’ siubhal gu ceann a deas nan Eilean Siar. The Hebridean Mermaid travels to the southern islands of the Outer Hebrides.

programme.title: Faodail
programme.desc: Tha Tasglann Fhilm Faodail a’ tarraing aire gu filmichean dhùthchasach Innse Gall bho na 1930an gu na 80an, a bha caillte ach a-nis glèidhte don ghinealach ri teachd. Tha bhana Cinema Sgìre Leantainneach a’ siubhal nan eilean, a’ taisbeanadh fhilmichean sna sgìrean ionadail, le cothrom am faicinn air-loidhne air feadh an t-saoghail. Cuirear aithris bheairteach ùr riutha, a’ buntainn ris a’ Ghàidhealtachd, airson luchd-amhairc an là an-diugh. The Faodail Film Archive celebrates lost indigenous film collections from the 1930s-1980s in the Outer Hebrides, preserving the archive for future generations. The Cinema Sgìre Continuing mobile cinema van travels the islands showcasing footage to local communities, making them accessible globally online and adding rich new narratives relevant to the Gàidhealtachd for contemporary audiences. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Transatlantic Sessions
programme.desc: Julie Fowlis agus Muireann Nic Amhlaoibh le taghadh ciùil bho Transatlantic Sessions. Julie Fowlis and Muireann Nic Amhlaoibh present highlights from Transatlantic Sessions.

programme.title: Marmalade le Gregor
programme.desc: Agus leis fhèin cho measail air marmalaid, tha Griogar a’ rannsachadh sgeul a’ bhidhe chlasaigeach seo. Marmalade fan Gregor Macleod explores the story of this classic preserve.

programme.title: Fraochy Bay
programme.desc: Là eile ann a Fraochy Bay agus tha sùilean cuid nas motha nam brù. Is ann caol a tha cuisean do dh'fhactaraidh pàidh Featherby's. Tha am fear leis am bheil e a cruthachadh farpais, feuch de am pàidh ùr a bheir an t-acras air na tha mun cuairt agus a chuireas sgillinn dhan a sporran. It's another day in Fraochy Bay and Featherby's Pie Factory has fallen on hard times. Owner Mr Featherby sets up a contest for one lucky person to choose a new pie flavour in order to boost his sales.

programme.title: Seòid a' Chidsin - The Kitchen Coves
programme.desc: ’S e deagh chòcairean a th’ anns na balaich. Air prògram an latha an-diugh, tha na seòid a’ feuchainn biadh bho thaobh sear na Roinn Eòrpa. Tha Ruaraidh a’ dèanamh Feòil-tunnaig Ròsta cuide ri bonnaich bhuntàta. Tha e cuideachd a’ sealltainn mar a nithear am brot traidiseanta, Borscht. Tha Ùisdean ag ullachadh teanga cuide ri glasraich picilte agus Sailead Olivier, a gheibhear san Ruis. Airson deireadh gnothaich, tha e a’ dèanamh mìlsean às an Ucràin – Solozhenik Ùbhlan. The lads cook Eastern European food. Roddy makes a roast duck accompanied by potato dumplings and also demonstrates a version of the classic Borscht soup. Meanwhile Uisdean cooks a tongue to be accompanied by pickled vegetables and the classic Russian olivier salad. To finish off, he creates a Ukrainian dessert, apple solozhenik. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: BBC Proms
programme.desc: More than 150 of the country's best young musicians take us on a metaphorical musical journey to the underworld and back under the watchful eye of conductor and composer Thomas Adès. Always a hotly anticipated highlight of any BBC Proms season, the National Youth Orchestra is at the Royal Albert Hall with a programme that opens with Liszt's intoxicating Mephisto Waltz No 1, a whirlwind score following the Faust legend as he waltzes out into the forest with a local village girl. Next up is a rare treat of a new piece conducted by the composer himself: Purgatorio–Dante ballet Part II is Thomas Adès’s contemplation of purgatory in this central act of his Grammy Award-winning ballet. To round off the concert, the orchestra delivers the dazzling Symphonie Fantastique by Berlioz. A vast young orchestra drenches the Royal Albert Hall in this mesmerising symphony. Presented by Petroc Trelawny.

programme.title: The Architecture the Railways Built
programme.desc: Tim Dunn explores disused tube station Down Street in Mayfair, which played a crucial tactical role during WWII, and tours Rotterdam Centraal station with its designer.

programme.title: The Flying Gardener
programme.desc: Chris Beardshaw visits inspirational gardens by helicopter. A look at fine examples of vertical gardening found in the castles and villages of the Cotswolds, plus climbing plants.

programme.title: Art of Spain
programme.desc: Critic and art historian Andrew Graham-Dixon travels from southern to northern Spain to tell the story of some of Europe's most exciting and vital art. He journeys to the country’s scorched centre to explore Spanish art of the 16th and 17th centuries. From the mystical world of El Greco to the tender genius of Velazquez, this was a moment so extraordinary it became known as the Golden Age. But beneath the glittering surface was a dark and savage heart. Travelling from the architectural jewel of Toledo to majestic Madrid, Andrew Graham-Dixon traces the rise and fall of the Spanish Empire, the brutal conquest of the New World, and the religious madness of the Inquisition, to discover how a history so violent could produce some of the most beautiful art ever seen.

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Magnus Magnusson hosts from Reading University. Specialist subjects include the Alps, symphony orchestra instruments, children's literature and the Old Testament.

programme.title: Call My Bluff
programme.desc: Robert Robinson chairs as team captains Frank Muir and Patrick Campbell are joined by Nanette Newman, Bryan Forbes, Joanna Lumley and Russell Harty.

programme.title: The Sky at Night
programme.desc: Professor Brian Cox joins the team to explore the mind-bending mysteries of black holes discovered by the James Webb Space Telescope’s most exciting new observations.

programme.title: Omnibus
programme.desc: Humphrey Burton examines the golden age of Spanish painting, originally broadcast in 1976 to coincide with a major exhibition at the Royal Academy of Arts.

programme.title: One Hundred Great Paintings
programme.desc: Edwin Mullins looks at Francisco de Zurbaran's Still Life with Lemons, Oranges and a Rose.

programme.title: Britain's Lost Waterlands: Escape to Swallows and Amazons Country
programme.desc: Documentary that follows presenters Dick Strawbridge and Alice Roberts as they explore the spectacular British landscapes that inspired children's author Arthur Ransome to write his series Swallows and Amazons. The landscapes he depicted are based on three iconic British waterlands. The beauty and drama of the Lake District shaped by ancient glaciers and rich in wildlife and natural resources, the shallow man-made waterways of the Norfolk broads so crucial to farming and reed production, and the coastal estuaries and deep-water harbours of the Suffolk coastline shaped by ferocious tides and crucial to trade. Engineer and keen sailor Dick uses vintage boats to explore the landscapes and meet people whose lives are shaped by the water, while wildlife enthusiast Alice explores the rich shorelines, interrogating the underlying geography and meeting the wildlife. Together they evoke the nostalgia of Ransome's writing and a bygone era of childhood freedom and adventure, but they also explore the economic significance of these special locations and the ways in which water was harnessed to change the course of British history.

Travelling from the architectural jewel of Toledo to majestic Madrid, Andrew Graham-Dixon traces the rise and fall of the Spanish Empire, the brutal conquest of the New World, and the religious madness of the Inquisition, to discover how a history so violent could produce some of the most beautiful art ever seen.

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Magnus Magnusson hosts from Reading University. Specialist subjects include the Alps, symphony orchestra instruments, children's literature and the Old Testament.

programme.title: Call My Bluff
programme.desc: Robert Robinson chairs as team captains Frank Muir and Patrick Campbell are joined by Nanette Newman, Bryan Forbes, Joanna Lumley and Russell Harty.

programme.title: The Sky at Night
programme.desc: Professor Brian Cox joins the team to explore the mind-bending mysteries of black holes discovered by the James Webb Space Telescope’s most exciting new observations.

programme.title: Omnibus
programme.desc: Humphrey Burton examines the golden age of Spanish painting, originally broadcast in 1976 to coincide with a major exhibition at the Royal Academy of Arts.

programme.title: One Hundred Great Paintings
programme.desc: Edwin Mullins looks at Francisco de Zurbaran's Still Life with Lemons, Oranges and a Rose.

programme.title: Britain's Lost Waterlands: Escape to Swallows and Amazons Country
programme.desc: Documentary that follows presenters Dick Strawbridge and Alice Roberts as they explore the spectacular British landscapes that inspired children's author Arthur Ransome to write his series Swallows and Amazons. The landscapes he depicted are based on three iconic British waterlands. The beauty and drama of the Lake District shaped by ancient glaciers and rich in wildlife and natural resources, the shallow man-made waterways of the Norfolk broads so crucial to farming and reed production, and the coastal estuaries and deep-water harbours of the Suffolk coastline shaped by ferocious tides and crucial to trade. Engineer and keen sailor Dick uses vintage boats to explore the landscapes and meet people whose lives are shaped by the water, while wildlife enthusiast Alice explores the rich shorelines, interrogating the underlying geography and meeting the wildlife. Together they evoke the nostalgia of Ransome's writing and a bygone era of childhood freedom and adventure, but they also explore the economic significance of these special locations and the ways in which water was harnessed to change the course of British history.

programme.title: The Flying Gardener
programme.desc: Chris Beardshaw visits inspirational gardens by helicopter. A look at fine examples of vertical gardening found in the castles and villages of the Cotswolds, plus climbing plants.

programme.title: Art of Spain
programme.desc: Critic and art historian Andrew Graham-Dixon travels from southern to northern Spain to tell the story of some of Europe's most exciting and vital art. He journeys to the country’s scorched centre to explore Spanish art of the 16th and 17th centuries. From the mystical world of El Greco to the tender genius of Velazquez, this was a moment so extraordinary it became known as the Golden Age. But beneath the glittering surface was a dark and savage heart. Travelling from the architectural jewel of Toledo to majestic Madrid, Andrew Graham-Dixon traces the rise and fall of the Spanish Empire, the brutal conquest of the New World, and the religious madness of the Inquisition, to discover how a history so violent could produce some of the most beautiful art ever seen.

programme.title: Breakfast

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: In Cheetah Kingdom, hopes are growing as Xena, the hand-reared female, might be pregnant. It’s a critical moment for the breeding programme and a deeply personal one for the team. Xena was rejected as a cub so the keepers had to step in, but having lacked a maternal role model, there are fears she might never be able to raise young of her own. Now all eyes are on Xena, but reading signs of pregnancy with cheetahs is incredibly difficult, and the next few weeks will be crucial. Elsewhere, Hamza films a strength-and-agility challenge in Lion Country. The team are encouraging the big cats to climb for their food, which creates a great opportunity to assess their physical condition. The lions scrambling up the trees raises an important survival tip: if one’s ever chasing you... maybe don’t climb a tree! Meanwhile, training continues over at the giraffe house. With medical checks on the horizon, the keepers are trying a new tactic: introducing the herd to a life-size cardboard cut-out of Ben. It might seem like a gimmick, but any change in the environment can trigger tension. Will ‘keeper’ Ben past the test?

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: Vehicle tracking specialists Neil and Jason are hunting down a missing hire car. The driver is refusing to give it back and has already racked up a staggering £3,000 in parking fines. Like most hire cars, it’s fitted with a tracker – so Neil and Jason, armed with a spare key, are planning to snatch it back. Meanwhile, it’s late at night when high-tech car thieves steal a BMW off a driveway in Warwick. But the car’s owner, Seb, hears them and is determined not to let them get away. He taps into the tracking app on his phone, picks up the signal from his car’s tracker and gives chase. At Felixstowe Port, intelligence officer Adam finds three high-value cars hidden under an assortment of junk, including old mattresses, sofas, footballs and even a kitchen sink. Adam checks the vehicles and discovers they’re all stolen.

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: The first ever European Athletics Championships to be held in Great Britain get under way in Birmingham, and it’s a busy first morning on the track and in the field. One of the fastest men in Europe over 800m this year, Max Burgin, is in action in qualifying and Dina Asher-Smith begins the defence of her 100m title. Jeanette Kwakye is joined in the studio by Jessica Ennis-Hill and Greg Rutherford. Commentary comes from Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe.

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: The first medals of the 2026 European Athletics Championships will be decided in Birmingham. Defending champion Dina Asher-Smith faces Amy Hunt in the final of the women’s 100m. Jakob Ingebrigtsen makes his comeback after almost a year out through injury in the men’s 5,000m final. Gabby Logan is joined in the studio by Greg Rutherford, Jessica Ennis-Hill and Jenny Meadows, with commentary from Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: In Cheetah Kingdom, hopes are growing as Xena, the hand-reared female, might be pregnant. It’s a critical moment for the breeding programme and a deeply personal one for the team. Xena was rejected as a cub so the keepers had to step in, but having lacked a maternal role model, there are fears she might never be able to raise young of her own. Now all eyes are on Xena, but reading signs of pregnancy with cheetahs is incredibly difficult, and the next few weeks will be crucial. Elsewhere, Hamza films a strength-and-agility challenge in Lion Country. The team are encouraging the big cats to climb for their food, which creates a great opportunity to assess their physical condition. The lions scrambling up the trees raises an important survival tip: if one’s ever chasing you... maybe don’t climb a tree! Meanwhile, training continues over at the giraffe house. With medical checks on the horizon, the keepers are trying a new tactic: introducing the herd to a life-size cardboard cut-out of Ben. It might seem like a gimmick, but any change in the environment can trigger tension. Will ‘keeper’ Ben past the test?

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: Vehicle tracking specialists Neil and Jason are hunting down a missing hire car. The driver is refusing to give it back and has already racked up a staggering £3,000 in parking fines. Like most hire cars, it’s fitted with a tracker – so Neil and Jason, armed with a spare key, are planning to snatch it back. Meanwhile, it’s late at night when high-tech car thieves steal a BMW off a driveway in Warwick. But the car’s owner, Seb, hears them and is determined not to let them get away. He taps into the tracking app on his phone, picks up the signal from his car’s tracker and gives chase. At Felixstowe Port, intelligence officer Adam finds three high-value cars hidden under an assortment of junk, including old mattresses, sofas, footballs and even a kitchen sink. Adam checks the vehicles and discovers they’re all stolen.

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: The first ever European Athletics Championships to be held in Great Britain get under way in Birmingham, and it’s a busy first morning on the track and in the field. One of the fastest men in Europe over 800m this year, Max Burgin, is in action in qualifying and Dina Asher-Smith begins the defence of her 100m title. Jeanette Kwakye is joined in the studio by Jessica Ennis-Hill and Greg Rutherford. Commentary comes from Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe.

programme.title: Escape to the Country

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: In Cheetah Kingdom, hopes are growing as Xena, the hand-reared female, might be pregnant. It’s a critical moment for the breeding programme and a deeply personal one for the team. Xena was rejected as a cub so the keepers had to step in, but having lacked a maternal role model, there are fears she might never be able to raise young of her own. Now all eyes are on Xena, but reading signs of pregnancy with cheetahs is incredibly difficult, and the next few weeks will be crucial. Elsewhere, Hamza films a strength-and-agility challenge in Lion Country. The team are encouraging the big cats to climb for their food, which creates a great opportunity to assess their physical condition. The lions scrambling up the trees raises an important survival tip: if one’s ever chasing you... maybe don’t climb a tree! Meanwhile, training continues over at the giraffe house. With medical checks on the horizon, the keepers are trying a new tactic: introducing the herd to a life-size cardboard cut-out of Ben. It might seem like a gimmick, but any change in the environment can trigger tension. Will ‘keeper’ Ben past the test?

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: Vehicle tracking specialists Neil and Jason are hunting down a missing hire car. The driver is refusing to give it back and has already racked up a staggering £3,000 in parking fines. Like most hire cars, it’s fitted with a tracker – so Neil and Jason, armed with a spare key, are planning to snatch it back. Meanwhile, it’s late at night when high-tech car thieves steal a BMW off a driveway in Warwick. But the car’s owner, Seb, hears them and is determined not to let them get away. He taps into the tracking app on his phone, picks up the signal from his car’s tracker and gives chase. At Felixstowe Port, intelligence officer Adam finds three high-value cars hidden under an assortment of junk, including old mattresses, sofas, footballs and even a kitchen sink. Adam checks the vehicles and discovers they’re all stolen.

programme.title: Girl Fight
programme.desc: Ballymena, County Antrim is home to Next Generation gym, where head coach Rodney Moore is on a mission to shape championship fighters from everyday people. Among them is amateur fighter Chloe Crozier, who has faced personal hardship and now has her sights set on turning pro. But after a number of tough losses, the question looms: can she prove she’s got what it takes to go pro and earn her place among the best in the cage? Also training at the gym is Rachel ‘The Diva’ McIlhagga, a rising talent who recently suffered a brutal defeat in an MMA bout. Her journey is one of rebuilding, physically and mentally, as she fights to reclaim her confidence and find her footing again. Girl Fight is a raw and intimate look at the lives of female fighters chasing transformation through combat. With every round, they face not just opponents but the weight of personal battles, self-doubt and the ever-present risk of injury. What drives ordinary women to step into the cage – and what does it take to walk out stronger?

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: In Cheetah Kingdom, hopes are growing as Xena, the hand-reared female, might be pregnant. It’s a critical moment for the breeding programme and a deeply personal one for the team. Xena was rejected as a cub so the keepers had to step in, but having lacked a maternal role model, there are fears she might never be able to raise young of her own. Now all eyes are on Xena, but reading signs of pregnancy with cheetahs is incredibly difficult, and the next few weeks will be crucial. Elsewhere, Hamza films a strength-and-agility challenge in Lion Country. The team are encouraging the big cats to climb for their food, which creates a great opportunity to assess their physical condition. The lions scrambling up the trees raises an important survival tip: if one’s ever chasing you... maybe don’t climb a tree! Meanwhile, training continues over at the giraffe house. With medical checks on the horizon, the keepers are trying a new tactic: introducing the herd to a life-size cardboard cut-out of Ben. It might seem like a gimmick, but any change in the environment can trigger tension. Will ‘keeper’ Ben past the test?

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: Vehicle tracking specialists Neil and Jason are hunting down a missing hire car. The driver is refusing to give it back and has already racked up a staggering £3,000 in parking fines. Like most hire cars, it’s fitted with a tracker – so Neil and Jason, armed with a spare key, are planning to snatch it back. Meanwhile, it’s late at night when high-tech car thieves steal a BMW off a driveway in Warwick. But the car’s owner, Seb, hears them and is determined not to let them get away. He taps into the tracking app on his phone, picks up the signal from his car’s tracker and gives chase. At Felixstowe Port, intelligence officer Adam finds three high-value cars hidden under an assortment of junk, including old mattresses, sofas, footballs and even a kitchen sink. Adam checks the vehicles and discovers they’re all stolen.

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: The first ever European Athletics Championships to be held in Great Britain get under way in Birmingham, and it’s a busy first morning on the track and in the field. One of the fastest men in Europe over 800m this year, Max Burgin, is in action in qualifying and Dina Asher-Smith begins the defence of her 100m title. Jeanette Kwakye is joined in the studio by Jessica Ennis-Hill and Greg Rutherford. Commentary comes from Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe.

programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: Are old plates valuable? It's a smashing skip find for Sarah Moore at Witley recycling centre in Surrey, but can she find a way to release the cash from this collection of china? Carpenter Ollie tries to launder a tidy profit from an old washstand, and husband and wife team Dani and Elliot have their hands full with sad seats in need of some TLC.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Travelling through the counties of Wiltshire and Somerset, Jonnie Irwin helps a pair of early retirees spend their whopping £1.3million budget on an impressive home in the countryside. They are after a characterful and spacious period property with at least four bedrooms and separate studies, but the most vital feature turns out to be sky high ceilings!

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: The first medals of the 2026 European Athletics Championships will be decided in Birmingham. Defending champion Dina Asher-Smith faces Amy Hunt in the final of the women’s 100m. Jakob Ingebrigtsen makes his comeback after almost a year out through injury in the men’s 5,000m final. And Great Britain will be amongst the favourites to claim the mixed 4 x 400m relay title, the first of six relay gold medals on offer this week. Gabby Logan is joined in the studio by Greg Rutherford, Jessica Ennis-Hill and Jenny Meadows, with commentary from Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: In Cheetah Kingdom, hopes are growing as Xena, the hand-reared female, might be pregnant. It’s a critical moment for the breeding programme and a deeply personal one for the team. Xena was rejected as a cub so the keepers had to step in, but having lacked a maternal role model, there are fears she might never be able to raise young of her own. Now all eyes are on Xena, but reading signs of pregnancy with cheetahs is incredibly difficult, and the next few weeks will be crucial. Elsewhere, Hamza films a strength-and-agility challenge in Lion Country. The team are encouraging the big cats to climb for their food, which creates a great opportunity to assess their physical condition. The lions scrambling up the trees raises an important survival tip: if one’s ever chasing you... maybe don’t climb a tree! Meanwhile, training continues over at the giraffe house. With medical checks on the horizon, the keepers are trying a new tactic: introducing the herd to a life-size cardboard cut-out of Ben. It might seem like a gimmick, but any change in the environment can trigger tension. Will ‘keeper’ Ben past the test?

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: Vehicle tracking specialists Neil and Jason are hunting down a missing hire car. The driver is refusing to give it back and has already racked up a staggering £3,000 in parking fines. Like most hire cars, it’s fitted with a tracker – so Neil and Jason, armed with a spare key, are planning to snatch it back. Meanwhile, it’s late at night when high-tech car thieves steal a BMW off a driveway in Warwick. But the car’s owner, Seb, hears them and is determined not to let them get away. He taps into the tracking app on his phone, picks up the signal from his car’s tracker and gives chase. At Felixstowe Port, intelligence officer Adam finds three high-value cars hidden under an assortment of junk, including old mattresses, sofas, footballs and even a kitchen sink. Adam checks the vehicles and discovers they’re all stolen.

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: The first ever European Athletics Championships to be held in Great Britain get under way in Birmingham, and it’s a busy first morning on the track and in the field. One of the fastest men in Europe over 800m this year, Max Burgin, is in action in qualifying and Dina Asher-Smith begins the defence of her 100m title. Jeanette Kwakye is joined in the studio by Jessica Ennis-Hill and Greg Rutherford. Commentary comes from Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: Are old plates valuable? It's a smashing skip find for Sarah Moore at Witley recycling centre in Surrey, but can she find a way to release the cash from this collection of china? programme.title: Escape to the Country

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: The first medals of the 2026 European Athletics Championships will be decided in Birmingham. Defending champion Dina Asher-Smith faces Amy Hunt in the final of the women’s 100m. Jakob Ingebrigtsen makes his comeback after almost a year out through injury in the men’s 5,000m final. And Great Britain will be amongst the favourites to claim the mixed 4 x 400m relay title, the first of six relay gold medals on offer this week. programme.title: The Great Food Guys
programme.desc: Chef Nick Nairn and Dougie Vipond celebrate the fantastic range of food and drink Scotland has to offer in their country kitchen. programme.title: The Mountain
programme.desc: The summer months bring new opportunities for the hardy folk who live in the shadow of Cairngorm. programme.title: The Mountain
programme.desc: The summer months bring new opportunities for the hardy folk who live in the shadow of Cairngorm. programme.title: Interior Design Masters with Alan Carr
programme.desc: It’s the quarter final, and Alan and the designers head to the UK’s 'town of books', Hay-on-Wye, in Wales, to transform two high-street shops. Working in pairs, they need to improve layout, footfall and visual merchandising before facing critiques from Michelle and retail expert Ross Bailey.

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: In Fife, it’s harvest time for Andy and Jo as they finally reap what they have sown. It has been a challenging year, and now it's time to discover just what last winter's wet weather might have cost them. With tensions about taking over the family farm subsiding, Nick and Holly are diversifying with a new cattle venture in Dumfries and Galloway. The whole family take their best easy-care sheep to auction in Carlisle. The Bakers are expanding their farm on Papa Westray and take delivery of a milking cow and calf to add to their ever-growing family.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Brian Cunningham’s beginner’s guide to vegetable growing started in April, and now it’s time to reap the rewards as he starts to harvest from the veg plot at Beechgrove Garden. Calum Clunie sows for winter crops as he starts the sowing cycle again on his family-sized plo. He also refreshes the containers he started in April as a demonstration of just what you can do if space is limited and you only room for some pots. Brian and Calum tackle Beechgrove’s hedges after checking carefully for bird nest activity, and Brian advises on caring for common houseplants. There is a visit to St Andrews Botanic Garden, along with the week’s handy hints.

programme.title: Paramedics on Scene
programme.desc: In Glasgow, Paul and Ryan of the Special Operations Response Team are called to a siege in a flat where a man has barricaded himself inside and is threatening to harm himself. It’s a difficult and emotional situation, and the team must coordinate with the police at the scene to try to ensure the best outcome. Meanwhile, Aberdeen-based teammates Kirsty and Bruce are called to see Rebecca, who has suffered an anaphylactic attack. The crew administer several doses of adrenaline, but Rebecca shows little signs of improvement, prompting a rapid journey on blue lights to Aberdeen Royal Infirmary. From the lowlands to the Highlands, the Scottish Air Ambulance Service delivers help to every part of the country. Serving as a paramedic on the King Air fixed-wing aircraft, Stephen travels to the Isle of Lewis. William is visiting the islands as part of a golfing holiday but has fractured his ribs in a fall, necessitating a transfer to the mainland.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Chi is rightfully asked if she’s ‘thick’ for bothering an electrician working on an out-of-order lift. For once in her life, Chi is forced to reconcile with her own intelligence. At her weekly grief counselling sessions, Ruth doesn’t exactly hold back, telling Chi she is indeed simple and not to bother seeking adult education. Chi sets out to prove her wrong and breaks into Ramsgate College in search of an education.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Chi’s ghost parents tell her she should really be worried about dying alone and encourage her to find a life partner. Chi casts a very wide and desperate net for potential love interests, approaching almost everyone in Ramsgate with her phone number. Meanwhile, Lucas gets a job at the cinema but is crumbling under the pressure and the perfectly normal expectations of his manager, Kenneth. Lucas resorts to stress-eating the pick ’n’ mix when nobody is looking.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: It’s Chi’s last free therapy session, and Ruth wants to know whether Chi can still see her dead parents or whether she’s learned anything at all from the counselling. But she very much can still see her dead parents; in fact, they were just in the hallway, wearing outdoor clothes and discussing what will become of them if they leave the house. Will they pass on to another plane? Will this be the end of them?

programme.title: BBC New Comedy Awards
programme.desc: The BBC's biggest comedy talent search is celebrating its 30th birthday, and we're heading to Bristol, where five comics will compete in the first of six knockout heats.

programme.title: BBC New Comedy Awards
programme.desc: Birmingham’s Hockley Social Club has been transformed into our very own comedy club. Taking to the stage are Eli Hart, Farhan Solo, Chloe Reynolds, Will BF and Monica Hsueh in a bid to impress our judges and book their place in the final. Award-winning comedian and writer Sarah Keyworth is here to keep the house in order. The judges are comedian, writer and podcaster Aurie Styla and local Brum stand-up Lindsey Santoro. Head judge Fatiha El-Ghorri completes the trio. It’s not going to be easy for them to pick a winner from the five new comics performing. With only five minutes on stage each, the sets are jam-packed with jokes and cutting-edge material, but only one can go through to the grand final in November at City of Culture 25 Bradford’s Alhambra Theatre.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Steve is in Uganda, getting up close and personal with some of our closest relatives - the primates. He meets gorillas in the mountains and squabbling baboons on the savannah. He even has a dawn encounter with chimps in the forest.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: The ten remaining sewers celebrate the rich fashion and textile traditions of Mexico. Host Sophie Willan and judges Patrick Grant and Esme Young are joined by a special guest judge, renowned fashion designer Erika Alvirez. In the Pattern Challenge, the sewers create a Mexican folkloric top using fabrics created by indigenous communities in Mexico’s Oaxaca region. For the Transformation Challenge, they are given manteles de hule, a traditional Mexican tablecloth. Using the stiffness of the fabric, they are asked to create a garment with an eye-catching structure. Finally, in the Made-to-Measure, the sewers design an outfit inspired by one of the many Mexican festivals found across the country.

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May are on a mission to build a bridge over the River Kwai in Thailand. However, in order to do that they must first drive across a country that has been largely closed to westerners for over 40 years: Burma. Furthermore, the trio must make this trip in three lorries that have been bought 'sight unseen' from the internet for a limited budget. Unsurprisingly, they are not quite as the trio might have hoped or expected. What follows is an epic journey of beautiful scenery, regular adversity, ongoing malfunction and the constant bickering of three badly dressed buffoons.

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May are battling across Burma in three ancient and barely functioning lorries. Having forded rivers, climbed mountains and endured a Burmese trucker stop, they must now venture into the Shan state, an area rife with civil war and normally closed to western TV crews, as they head towards Thailand and their final challenge - to build a bridge over the River Kwai.

programme.title: Tommy: The Good. The Bad. The Fury
programme.desc: It is Tommy’s birthday, but there is no time for cake. With just days to go before his long-awaited comeback fight in Budapest, Tommy is pulled in every direction, juggling press conferences, promo shoots and the pressure of proving he has still got what it takes in the ring. Fighting on the same bill as his older brother Roman, Tommy steps into the spotlight once again and puts himself to the test against a hard-hitting Bosnian heavyweight. In a high-stakes bout that could define his future, Tommy isn’t just fighting for his career - he is fighting for the life he is desperate to rebuild. Meanwhile, there is a more personal battle quietly playing out at home. With the house freshly prepared for Molly-Mae and Bambi’s return, Tommy hopes he has done enough to prove he has changed. But now that he may have won them back, can he keep them?

programme.title: Tommy: The Good. The Bad. The Fury
programme.desc: After the success of his comeback fight, Tommy’s road to redemption hits a major setback - his hand is injured again and needs eight weeks’ total rest before doctors will know if he can fight again. The last time he couldn’t train, his life spiralled out of control, so now Tommy throws himself into a frenzy of activity: a TV appearance on The Wheel, family days out with Bambi, and a final push to finish the home he hopes Molly and Bambi will soon return to. In search of focus and inspiration, Tommy heads to Marbella to train with his childhood hero - legendary bodybuilder Dorian Yates. But in a world of yacht trips, sun-soaked distractions and luxury villas, can Tommy stay disciplined and keep his relationship and boxing career back on track? As doubts grow over his recovery, Tommy faces the toughest question of all - is this just a setback or the beginning of the end of his boxing career?

programme.title: Tommy: The Good. The Bad. The Fury
programme.desc: Tommy’s recovery is back on track after he and John put his hand to the test. The pair are training again, and the search for Tommy’s next opponent begins. Eager to make the most of family time, Tommy splashes out on a £90,000 motor home for family trips with Molly and Bambi and takes his mum out for lunch and a long-overdue catch-up. Tommy reveals that John has had a recent health scare, so to cheer him up, father and son take their very different caravans to a local steam fair. It’s vital for Tommy’s mental health that he keeps physically active at all times, so he sets his sights on an ambitious new goal - a 100km triathlon. Meanwhile, John worries that the physical toll from this could jeopardise the chances of Tommy recovering and landing a big money fight. As Tommy throws himself into training for the triathlon, one question remains - can he avoid getting injured, or will this new challenge end his boxing career for good?

programme.title: Tommy: The Good. The Bad. The Fury
programme.desc: Tommy realises just how far he and Molly have come since their separation last year, but John’s worries grow as Tommy takes on a 100km triathlon, pushing his body to new physical limits. Before the challenge, Tommy takes some downtime at the spa with his mates, preparing for a huge press push ahead of his series premiere. He’s come a long way since he and Molly separated last year, and the truth hits home when he sees his face on a billboard - and shares the moment with Molly. The premiere brings together family and friends, all celebrating how far Tommy has come. But there’s no time to rest - he heads to the south of France for the triathlon, where Molly and Bambi surprise him at the finishing line. Even with the triathlon behind him, Tommy’s pursuit of physical challenges continues as he gears up for the Great North Run the following week. Riding a high, he is suddenly hit with a backlash on social media, leaving him to wonder what he can do to catch a break.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Chi is rightfully asked if she’s ‘thick’ for bothering an electrician working on an out-of-order lift. For once in her life, Chi is forced to reconcile with her own intelligence. At her weekly grief counselling sessions, Ruth doesn’t exactly hold back, telling Chi she is indeed simple and not to bother seeking adult education. Chi sets out to prove her wrong and breaks into Ramsgate College in search of an education.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Chi’s ghost parents tell her she should really be worried about dying alone and encourage her to find a life partner. Chi casts a very wide and desperate net for potential love interests, approaching almost everyone in Ramsgate with her phone number. Meanwhile, Lucas gets a job at the cinema but is crumbling under the pressure and the perfectly normal expectations of his manager, Kenneth. programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are?
programme.desc: Harriet Walter delves into her family history, discovering ancestors who are just as colourful as some of fictional characters she has played on stage and screen. In a journey that takes her from Whitehall to Italy to Australia, she follows in the footsteps of her ancestors, including her flamboyant Italian great-great-grandfather Girolamo Carindini, an Italian aristocrat who fled into exile and settled in Tasmania. Here, he married Australia’s first opera diva. But drama and trouble followed Girolamo as he made as many headlines for his appearances in the debtor’s court as he did for his theatrical performances.

programme.title: Ann Droid
programme.desc: Sue has invited Michael and Renee to a nice family dinner in an attempt to play happy families, which means she can’t accept Phyllis’s invite to her surprise birthday party. Michael and Renee’s real motive for coming round is revealed, and things take a turn for the worst. Fortunately, Linda is there to avert tragedy and reveal the biggest shock of the night.

programme.title: The Devil in the Family: The Fall of Ruby Franke
programme.desc: With the family increasingly isolated, the home begins to draw unwanted attention. When a lucky escape exposes Ruby and Jodi’s world, the truth proves far worse than anyone imagined.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Danny visits The One Show studio, where Alex Jones and Roman Kemp reveal their love of antiques and collectibles. In Builth Wells, two teams of well-known faces search for bargains.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: Kev's in hot water! Boiling, in fact, as he wrestles with a rusty water tank. Upholsterer Larissa needs to find a way of getting a tired set of dining chairs sitting pretty again. And Jacqui Joseph takes on her biggest challenge to date, a massive display unit, but will she manage to make it fit for a modern home?

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc: It’s a family affair as Steve Fletcher fixes a model watermill while son Fred brings a cherished clock back to life. The team also fix a stunning Notting Hill Carnival headpiece.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: Margie Cooper and Tim Medhurst are reunited. Our Cheshire-based silver expert beat the Dorset-dwelling coin guru last time they were paired a few years ago. Margie's keen to do it again, while Tim is playing for pride, pleasure and, of course, profits. They start out in Blackpool, and this time the wheels will be an electric-powered 1970 crew cab fire engine. Can they set the saleroom ablaze when they go head-to-head?

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A father and daughter duo build three stunning townhouses in Eastbourne, boasting lovely views, while developers in Bilston and Croydon transform an existing terrace and flat into smart modern homes.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Charlie Ross and the teams are in Shropshire. Experts Charles Hanson and Ben Cooper lead the reds and blues as they compete for bargains at an antiques fair in Oswestry. Meanwhile, Charlie visits a family firm in Llangollen who are crafting wood to make standing frames for people with spinal injuries.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Mehreen Baig, Clare Balding, Jamie Laing and Mike Wozniak take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted by the House of Games reusable coffee mug, which is brand new for this series?

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp and his sidekick Sarah Greene host this quiz show, where the contestants race on moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers stop them in their tracks. Five contestants battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races, where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Do You Know Your Place?
programme.desc: Vernon Kay is at the helm of this quiz all about the UK. The Traitors star Paul Gorton leads an unreliable tour of a different destination each day, with celebrity players battling it out to sort unbelievable facts from fiction. This week’s guests are EastEnders star Nitin Ganatra, the Reverend Kate Bottley and Gladiator Apollo, aka Alex Gray. The tour starts in Derry/Londonderry. A daily winner is declared at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned.

programme.title: The Farmers' Country Showdown
programme.desc: Livestock farmer Lyn is proud that her sons, Thomas and Jack, have inherited her passion for rearing and promoting rare-breed animals. It means running their North Yorkshire farm is a family effort. However, they are all preparing for stiff competition against each other at the Staffordshire County Show. With their own different rare-breed flocks, Jack has high hopes that he will beat his mum in the show ring when his spiralled-horned Boreray meets her four-horned Manx Loaghtan. Meanwhile, Jersey cattle farming couple Jan and David, and his daughter Fiona, are just as determined to bag themselves a row of rosettes for their Shropshire farm. David has competed at the Staffordshire County Show for nearly 40 years and is confident he knows how to become a champion. They have each picked their favourite cow and will all go head-to-head in the show ring. However, Fiona’s got a job on her hands dealing with her grumpy Jersey.

programme.title: Spy in the Ocean
programme.desc: Spy creatures reveal an ocean full of startling ways of thinking, including the largest brain, smart octopi, diving monkeys, creative masterminds and other intriguing intelligence.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the experts visit the gardens of Chartwell in Kent, the former home of Sir Winston Churchill, where they are shown a painting by Graham Sutherland found behind a water tank. There is also a Gainsborough portrait, a collection of signatures by Battle of Britain pilots stationed at Biggin Hill, and a Russian sub-machine gun owned by a vicar.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin revisits some of the locations visited by Flog It! and presents all-new valuations. Experts touch down at Bletchley Park, the Ulster Transport Museum and Crowcombe Court to track down some unusual items to sell at auction. They uncover a beautiful watercolour and some stunning porcelain, and Paul Martin visits Antony in Cornwall to unearth a fascinating family history.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Chris Bisson, Danielle Harold, Katharine Merry and Robert Webb take on a series of rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games retro bag?

programme.title: Bear Grylls - Wild Reckoning
programme.desc: Former best friends Rhys and Niall come together in the wild to see if they can repair their relationship after barely speaking for the last two years. Their friendship faltered after the death of Niall’s older brother, when grief left him feeling withdrawn from those around him, and Rhys was unsure how best to reach out. The pair are set a canoeing challenge, and side by side, they also take on a forward-facing abseil down a sheer cliff face. In a campfire chat with mediator Mo, the pair talk for the first time about the reasons they drifted apart, confront past hurts and share the pain of bereavement. Will these two days be enough to rebuild the trust and friendship they once shared?

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: Five gold medals will be awarded in the first evening session of the European Athletics Championships as the women’s shot put final gets underway. There’s also qualifying for the women’s 100m hurdles. This is the first time that Great Britain has ever hosted these Championships, and there are over 1,600 athletes from 48 countries taking part. Gabby Logan is joined in the studio by Jessica Ennis-Hill, Jenny Meadows and Greg Rutherford, and they reflect on all the action from the morning session as well as previewing the women’s 100m final. Commentary comes from Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe.

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Victoria Coren Mitchell hosts the quiz where knowledge only gets you so far – the vital extra ingredients are logic and lateral thinking. Three Rocky Horror fans take on a team of New Zealanders, trying to establish the connection between such clues as back save, leg help, face accept the reality and knees party. One of the teams worked it out after three clues – but what is the answer?

programme.title: University Challenge
programme.desc: The heats continue, with Magdalen College, Oxford, facing Warwick for a place in the second round. Amol Rajan asks the questions.

programme.title: Evolution
programme.desc: How did the horse become so fast? Chris Packham sets out on a slithering, swimming, sprinting odyssey that explores the evolutionary beginnings of animal movement and how it reached its peak in one of the most elegant and athletic animals on earth: the horse.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul and Bob venture from London to the Scottish Highlands, taking a sleeper train overnight to their destination. They wake in the stunning vista of north west Scotland, where the pine forests and snow-topped mountains almost take their breath away. They are on a quest to fish for ferox trout, which is a tall order for any angler. But they are in the right place, the River Garry, with a local guide to help them target their quarry. Setting off in a boat, the pair fish long and hard, while also taking time to look for the Loch Ness monster.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the crucial news stories of the day. With Alex Forsyth.

programme.title: Shaft
programme.desc: Private detective John Shaft, hired by Harlem gangster Bumpy Jonas to rescue his kidnapped daughter, is secretly under pressure to investigate Jonas's criminal activities.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: In the first of four special episodes, Adam Henson meets a new generation of farmers navigating the challenges and opportunities of producing our food. Along the way, Adam gets a glimpse into their daily lives, exploring how they are facing the growing uncertainty in the industry and seeing what innovations they have embraced to secure the future of their farms. Travelling to Bala in Gwynedd, north Wales, he meets 23-year-old sheep and cattle farmer Erin McNaught. A fourth-generation farmer, Erin manages around 250 acres across three sites in partnership with her grandfather. Adam joins her on the daily rounds to discover the realities of running a traditional hill farm and hears how she is balancing the responsibility of carrying on a family legacy with the need to build a resilient business for the future. Adam also looks back through the show's archives at some of the inspirational young farmers we have met across the UK.

programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Mehreen Baig, Clare Balding, Jamie Laing and Mike Wozniak take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted by the House of Games reusable coffee mug, which is brand new for this series?

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp and his sidekick Sarah Greene host this quiz show, where the contestants race on moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers stop them in their tracks. Five contestants battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races, where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Do You Know Your Place?
programme.desc: Vernon Kay is at the helm of this quiz all about the UK. The Traitors star Paul Gorton leads an unreliable tour of a different destination each day, with celebrity players battling it out to sort unbelievable facts from fiction. This week’s guests are EastEnders star Nitin Ganatra, the Reverend Kate Bottley and Gladiator Apollo, aka Alex Gray. The tour starts in Derry/Londonderry. A daily winner is declared at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned.

programme.title: The Farmers' Country Showdown
programme.desc: Livestock farmer Lyn is proud that her sons, Thomas and Jack, have inherited her passion for rearing and promoting rare-breed animals. It means running their North Yorkshire farm is a family effort. However, they are all preparing for stiff competition against each other at the Staffordshire County Show. With their own different rare-breed flocks, Jack has high hopes that he will beat his mum in the show ring when his spiralled-horned Boreray meets her four-horned Manx Loaghtan. Meanwhile, Jersey cattle farming couple Jan and David, and his daughter Fiona, are just as determined to bag themselves a row of rosettes for their Shropshire farm. David has competed at the Staffordshire County Show for nearly 40 years and is confident he knows how to become a champion. They have each picked their favourite cow and will all go head-to-head in the show ring. However, Fiona’s got a job on her hands dealing with her grumpy Jersey.

programme.title: Spy in the Ocean
programme.desc: Spy creatures reveal an ocean full of startling ways of thinking, including the largest brain, smart octopi, diving monkeys, creative masterminds and other intriguing intelligence.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the experts visit the gardens of Chartwell in Kent, the former home of Sir Winston Churchill, where they are shown a painting by Graham Sutherland found behind a water tank. There is also a Gainsborough portrait, a collection of signatures by Battle of Britain pilots stationed at Biggin Hill, and a Russian sub-machine gun owned by a vicar.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin revisits some of the locations visited by Flog It! and presents all-new valuations. Experts touch down at Bletchley Park, the Ulster Transport Museum and Crowcombe Court to track down some unusual items to sell at auction. They uncover a beautiful watercolour and some stunning porcelain, and Paul Martin visits Antony in Cornwall to unearth a fascinating family history.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Chris Bisson, Danielle Harold, Katharine Merry and Robert Webb take on a series of rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games retro bag?

programme.title: Bear Grylls - Wild Reckoning
programme.desc: Former best friends Rhys and Niall come together in the wild to see if they can repair their relationship after barely speaking for the last two years. Their friendship faltered after the death of Niall’s older brother, when grief left him feeling withdrawn from those around him, and Rhys was unsure how best to reach out. The pair are set a canoeing challenge, and side by side, they also take on a forward-facing abseil down a sheer cliff face. In a campfire chat with mediator Mo, the pair talk for the first time about the reasons they drifted apart, confront past hurts and share the pain of bereavement. Will these two days be enough to rebuild the trust and friendship they once shared?

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: Five gold medals will be awarded in the first evening session of the European Athletics Championships as the women’s shot put final gets underway. There’s also qualifying for the women’s 100m hurdles. This is the first time that Great Britain has ever hosted these Championships, and there are over 1,600 athletes from 48 countries taking part. Gabby Logan is joined in the studio by Jessica Ennis-Hill, Jenny Meadows and Greg Rutherford, and they reflect on all the action from the morning session as well as previewing the women’s 100m final. Commentary comes from Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe.

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Victoria Coren Mitchell hosts the quiz where knowledge only gets you so far – the vital extra ingredients are logic and lateral thinking. Three Rocky Horror fans take on a team of New Zealanders, trying to establish the connection between such clues as back save, leg help, face accept the reality and knees party. One of the teams worked it out after three clues – but what is the answer?

programme.title: University Challenge
programme.desc: The heats continue, with Magdalen College, Oxford, facing Warwick for a place in the second round. Amol Rajan asks the questions.

programme.title: Evolution
programme.desc: How did the horse become so fast? Chris Packham sets out on a slithering, swimming, sprinting odyssey that explores the evolutionary beginnings of animal movement and how it reached its peak in one of the most elegant and athletic animals on earth: the horse.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul and Bob venture from London to the Scottish Highlands, taking a sleeper train overnight to their destination. They wake in the stunning vista of north west Scotland, where the pine forests and snow-topped mountains almost take their breath away. They are on a quest to fish for ferox trout, which is a tall order for any angler. But they are in the right place, the River Garry, with a local guide to help them target their quarry. Setting off in a boat, the pair fish long and hard, while also taking time to look for the Loch Ness monster.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the crucial news stories of the day. With Alex Forsyth.

programme.title: Shaft
programme.desc: Private detective John Shaft, hired by Harlem gangster Bumpy Jonas to rescue his kidnapped daughter, is secretly under pressure to investigate Jonas's criminal activities.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: In the first of four special episodes, Adam Henson meets a new generation of farmers navigating the challenges and opportunities of producing our food. Along the way, Adam gets a glimpse into their daily lives, exploring how they are facing the growing uncertainty in the industry and seeing what innovations they have embraced to secure the future of their farms. Travelling to Bala in Gwynedd, north Wales, he meets 23-year-old sheep and cattle farmer Erin McNaught. A fourth-generation farmer, Erin manages around 250 acres across three sites in partnership with her grandfather. Adam joins her on the daily rounds to discover the realities of running a traditional hill farm and hears how she is balancing the responsibility of carrying on a family legacy with the need to build a resilient business for the future. Adam also looks back through the show's archives at some of the inspirational young farmers we have met across the UK.

programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are?
programme.desc: Harriet Walter delves into her family history, discovering ancestors who are just as colourful as some of fictional characters she has played on stage and screen. In a journey that takes her from Whitehall to Italy to Australia, she follows in the footsteps of her ancestors, including her flamboyant Italian great-great-grandfather Girolamo Carindini, an Italian aristocrat who fled into exile and settled in Tasmania. Here, he married Australia’s first opera diva. But drama and trouble followed Girolamo as he made as many headlines for his appearances in the debtor’s court as he did for his theatrical performances.

programme.title: Ann Droid
programme.desc: Sue has invited Michael and Renee to a nice family dinner in an attempt to play happy families, which means she can’t accept Phyllis’s invite to her surprise birthday party. Michael and Renee’s real motive for coming round is revealed, and things take a turn for the worst. Fortunately, Linda is there to avert tragedy and reveal the biggest shock of the night.

programme.title: The Devil in the Family: The Fall of Ruby Franke
programme.desc: With the family increasingly isolated, the home begins to draw unwanted attention. When a lucky escape exposes Ruby and Jodi’s world, the truth proves far worse than anyone imagined.

programme.desc: Kev's in hot water! Boiling, in fact, as he wrestles with a rusty water tank. Upholsterer Larissa needs to find a way of getting a tired set of dining chairs sitting pretty again. programme.title: Do You Know Your Place?
programme.desc: Vernon Kay is at the helm of this quiz all about the UK. A daily winner is declared at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned.

programme.title: The Farmers' Country Showdown
programme.desc: Livestock farmer Lyn is proud that her sons, Thomas and Jack, have inherited her passion for rearing and promoting rare-breed animals. It means running their North Yorkshire farm is a family effort. However, they are all preparing for stiff competition against each other at the Staffordshire County Show. With their own different rare-breed flocks, Jack has high hopes that he will beat his mum in the show ring when his spiralled-horned Boreray meets her four-horned Manx Loaghtan. Meanwhile, Jersey cattle farming couple Jan and David, and his daughter Fiona, are just as determined to bag themselves a row of rosettes for their Shropshire farm. David has competed at the Staffordshire County Show for nearly 40 years and is confident he knows how to become a champion. They have each picked their favourite cow and will all go head-to-head in the show ring. However, Fiona’s got a job on her hands dealing with her grumpy Jersey.

programme.title: Spy in the Ocean
programme.desc: Spy creatures reveal an ocean full of startling ways of thinking, including the largest brain, smart octopi, diving monkeys, creative masterminds and other intriguing intelligence.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the experts visit the gardens of Chartwell in Kent, the former home of Sir Winston Churchill, where they are shown a painting by Graham Sutherland found behind a water tank. There is also a Gainsborough portrait, a collection of signatures by Battle of Britain pilots stationed at Biggin Hill, and a Russian sub-machine gun owned by a vicar.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin revisits some of the locations visited by Flog It! and presents all-new valuations. Experts touch down at Bletchley Park, the Ulster Transport Museum and Crowcombe Court to track down some unusual items to sell at auction. They uncover a beautiful watercolour and some stunning porcelain, and Paul Martin visits Antony in Cornwall to unearth a fascinating family history.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Chris Bisson, Danielle Harold, Katharine Merry and Robert Webb take on a series of rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games retro bag?

programme.title: Bear Grylls - Wild Reckoning
programme.desc: Former best friends Rhys and Niall come together in the wild to see if they can repair their relationship after barely speaking for the last two years. Their friendship faltered after the death of Niall’s older brother, when grief left him feeling withdrawn from those around him, and Rhys was unsure how best to reach out. The pair are set a canoeing challenge, and side by side, they also take on a forward-facing abseil down a sheer cliff face. In a campfire chat with mediator Mo, the pair talk for the first time about the reasons they drifted apart, confront past hurts and share the pain of bereavement. Will these two days be enough to rebuild the trust and friendship they once shared?

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: Five gold medals will be awarded in the first evening session of the European Athletics Championships as the women’s shot put final gets underway. There’s also qualifying for the women’s 100m hurdles. This is the first time that Great Britain has ever hosted these Championships, and there are over 1,600 athletes from 48 countries taking part. Gabby Logan is joined in the studio by Jessica Ennis-Hill, Jenny Meadows and Greg Rutherford, and they reflect on all the action from the morning session as well as previewing the women’s 100m final. Commentary comes from Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe.

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Victoria Coren Mitchell hosts the quiz where knowledge only gets you so far – the vital extra ingredients are logic and lateral thinking. Three Rocky Horror fans take on a team of New Zealanders, trying to establish the connection between such clues as back save, leg help, face accept the reality and knees party. One of the teams worked it out after three clues – but what is the answer?

programme.title: University Challenge
programme.desc: The heats continue, with Magdalen College, Oxford, facing Warwick for a place in the second round. Amol Rajan asks the questions.

programme.title: Evolution
programme.desc: How did the horse become so fast? Chris Packham sets out on a slithering, swimming, sprinting odyssey that explores the evolutionary beginnings of animal movement and how it reached its peak in one of the most elegant and athletic animals on earth: the horse.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul and Bob venture from London to the Scottish Highlands, taking a sleeper train overnight to their destination. They wake in the stunning vista of north west Scotland, where the pine forests and snow-topped mountains almost take their breath away. They are on a quest to fish for ferox trout, which is a tall order for any angler. But they are in the right place, the River Garry, with a local guide to help them target their quarry. Setting off in a boat, the pair fish long and hard, while also taking time to look for the Loch Ness monster.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the crucial news stories of the day. With Alex Forsyth.

programme.title: Shaft
programme.desc: Private detective John Shaft, hired by Harlem gangster Bumpy Jonas to rescue his kidnapped daughter, is secretly under pressure to investigate Jonas's criminal activities.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: In the first of four special episodes, Adam Henson meets a new generation of farmers navigating the challenges and opportunities of producing our food. Along the way, Adam gets a glimpse into their daily lives, exploring how they are facing the growing uncertainty in the industry and seeing what innovations they have embraced to secure the future of their farms. Travelling to Bala in Gwynedd, north Wales, he meets 23-year-old sheep and cattle farmer Erin McNaught. A fourth-generation farmer, Erin manages around 250 acres across three sites in partnership with her grandfather. Adam joins her on the daily rounds to discover the realities of running a traditional hill farm and hears how she is balancing the responsibility of carrying on a family legacy with the need to build a resilient business for the future. Adam also looks back through the show's archives at some of the inspirational young farmers we have met across the UK.

programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are?
programme.desc: Harriet Walter delves into her family history, discovering ancestors who are just as colourful as some of fictional characters she has played on stage and screen. In a journey that takes her from Whitehall to Italy to Australia, she follows in the footsteps of her ancestors, including her flamboyant Italian great-great-grandfather Girolamo Carindini, an Italian aristocrat who fled into exile and settled in Tasmania. Here, he married Australia’s first opera diva. But drama and trouble followed Girolamo as he made as many headlines for his appearances in the debtor’s court as he did for his theatrical performances.

programme.title: Ann Droid
programme.desc: Sue has invited Michael and Renee to a nice family dinner in an attempt to play happy families, which means she can’t accept Phyllis’s invite to her surprise birthday party. Michael and Renee’s real motive for coming round is revealed, and things take a turn for the worst. Fortunately, Linda is there to avert tragedy and reveal the biggest shock of the night.

programme.title: The Devil in the Family: The Fall of Ruby Franke
programme.desc: With the family increasingly isolated, the home begins to draw unwanted attention. When a lucky escape exposes Ruby and Jodi’s world, the truth proves far worse than anyone imagined.

programme.title: Hey Duggee

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: Mojo and Bo were supposed to paint fresh lines on the street. But when they get into a race with Tao, the paint goes in every direction, causing wild traffic chaos.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Bing and Coco are drawing Gilly a picture. When she and Popsie arrive, Bing goes to say hello, but while he does so Charlie makes a big squiggle on Bing's drawing!
